rows.abstract_level_claim: Anti-unification computes the least general generalization of two terms: their most-specific common pattern, with variables at disagreement positions.
rows.title: J. C. Reynolds 1970, Minsky Festschrift: 'Transformational Systems and the Algebraic Structure of Atomic Formulas'

rows.abstract_level_claim: Cited by #214 section 1. Top-down library learning: search for the single abstraction with maximum usefulness (compression achieved), rewrite the corpus with it, repeat. Anti-unification inside; no neural guide required.
rows.functional_reading: library learning <- anti-unification + usefulness-driven top-down search (Stitch)
rows.title: Bowers, Newton, Ragan-Kelley, Cheung, Solar-Lezama, POPL 2023: 'Top-Down Synthesis for Library Learning'

rows.abstract_level_claim: Equality saturation: represent all rewrites of a term in one e-graph (union-find over e-classes), saturate under a node/rule budget, then extract a minimum-cost program. Cited by #214 section 1.
rows.title: Willsey, Nandi, Wang, Tatlock, Popham 2021: 'egg: Fast and Extensible Equality Saturation'

rows.abstract_level_claim: Macro-operators: reusable action sequences learned from solved problems, traded between search depth and branching factor.
rows.functional_reading: composition reuse <- macro-operator learning (Korf 1985, predecessor of library learning in search)
rows.title: R. E. Korf 1985, Artificial Intelligence 24: 'Macro-Operators: A Weak Method for Learning'

rows.abstract_level_claim: Chunking: when a goal is achieved, build a production whose conditions are the goal differences that held and whose action is the subgoal result. Cited by #214 section 4 FNA-4 as the cognitive-architecture parent. Exact-difference conditions, no abstraction over arguments.
rows.title: Soar manual, section 4: 'Procedural Knowledge and Learning' (Laird, Rosenbloom, Newell lineage)

rows.abstract_level_claim: Counterexample-guided inductive synthesis: a verifier supplies counterexamples that refine a candidate until it passes; no gradient signal. Cited by #214 section 1 and section 4 FNA-4.
rows.title: Solar-Lezama, CEGIS lecture notes (Synthesis Course 2020, Lecture 10)

rows.abstract_level_claim: DreamCoder's library component grows abstractions from a wake/sleep loop in which a neural guide proposes which fragments to abstract. #214 section 4 FNA-4 explicitly requires the neural guide removed/ablated where possible: the remaining mechanism is anti-unification + utility scoring, i.e. the Stitch parent.
rows.functional_reading: DreamCoder minus neural guide == Stitch parent; the neural part is the donor under test, not the parent
rows.title: Ellis et al. 2021: 'DreamCoder: Bootstrapping Inductive Program Synthesis with Wake-Sleep Library Learning'
